blocks.text: Nitrification and denitrification are the two phases of the nitrogen cycle. Nitrification involves the conversion of ammonium (NH₄¹⁺) to nitrite (NO₂¹⁻) and nitrate (NO₃¹⁻), while denitrification involves the conversion of nitrate (NO₃¹⁻) to Nitrogen (N₂). These two processes are also involved in the wastewater treatment to remove nitrogen. Some differences between nitrification and denitrification are given in Table 12.2.

blocks.prompt: a) Write down the reduction and oxidation reactions that occur in the catalytic converter in the vehicle exhausts.
blocks.explanation:
Reduction: 2NO + 2CO → N₂ + 2CO₂ (Pt/Rh)
Oxidation: 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂, and oxidation of hydrocarbons, for example 2C₂H₄ + 6O₂ → 4CO₂ + 4H₂O

blocks.prompt: b) What is the basic principle of catalytic converter? Describe the role of catalyst in the catalytic converter.
blocks.explanation: The hot exhaust gases pass through honeycomb channels whose alumina coating carries Pt, Pd and Rh with a large surface area. The gases are adsorbed on this surface and react quickly: NO is reduced to N₂, and CO and hydrocarbons are oxidized to CO₂ and water. The catalyst lowers the activation energy and is not used up.

blocks.prompt: c) Do hybrid and electric cars have catalytic converters? Explain why or why not.
blocks.explanation: A hybrid car also has a petrol engine, which produces exhaust gases, so it has a catalytic converter. A fully electric car burns no fuel and produces no exhaust gas, so it does not need one.
